title: Use cases beyond deploying a model
verdict: Against "do anything I tell it, learn it once, repeat it from chat or the API, and keep it running", this area is at the start: everything Spark Console can change is a chat-model server on Spark 3 or 4. I checked the four limits the conclusions rest on in the code: one console model per Spark on port 8000, a done-check that accepts only a chat or completion answer, healing that returns unless the container is a model, and a rule that nothing but the brain starts on Spark 2. The parts that make repetition work already exist (typed actions, saved workflows, POST /actions/<name>, carry-on turns), so the missing piece is narrow: one saved "workload" description with two kinds (a service that stays up, a job that finishes), three actions, and healing for them. With that, a first-time request becomes: look up a guide, save the description, one yes from the owner, verified; after that it is a name that works from chat, the API or a workflow step. About two weeks of work covers gaps 1 to 5; GPU services, a port per model, file transfer and extra gateway paths should wait until a real use asks for them, and the contract's pipelines, dev boxes, queues and app store are not worth building for one owner. Nothing proposed touches SSH, Tailscale, the firewall, users or the brain; the one real hazard is a GPU workload freezing Spark 3 or 4, because container limits reportedly do not bound GPU memory on these machines, which is why GPU work never goes on Spark 2.
worksToday: Chat LLMs and vision models on Spark 3 and 4, alone or split across both over the cable: start_model finds, downloads, places, picks the best known setup, checks it answers and retries known failures (17-changes.mjs:496-515).

Seeing everything: the `workloads` read lists every container on every Spark, including hand-started services, labelled model, service, sparkie or other (19-watcher.mjs:57, 16-actions.mjs:770), and container_logs reads any container.
Repeating by name: save_workflow and run_workflow chain up to 12 existing actions with {inputs}, and run from chat, the agent door or a workflow step (18-workflows.mjs:147-203).

POST /actions/<name> runs any action as the owner's own call, and /v1 passes chat, completions, responses, embeddings and rerank. Both are in service/src now (24-handler.mjs:224-228, 15-routes.mjs:144); whether they are installed on Spark 2 I did not check.
Sparkie carries a multi-step request on after its operations finish, up to 8 turns and 2 hours (14-chats.mjs:127-141; built, in the test gate).
Healing for models: a crashed one-Spark model, a lost part of a two-Spark model, what should run after a power-on, and a silent brain (18-workflows.mjs:244-280, 20-heal.mjs).
The fence a sandbox needs is already there: calls from the Sparks' own addresses are refused outside /v1 (24-handler.mjs:44) and never start a model (15-routes.mjs, the fromSpark check).
A run-to-completion container already exists as a pattern: the Hugging Face download runs Python inside an engine image with `docker run --rm` (11-setups.mjs:397).
Memory safety on start: 8 GB of each Spark is always kept free and a model that doesn't fit is refused (05-library.mjs:297-310).

gaps.gap: Only model servers can be started. There is no way to run a service (search, a vector store, any container with a port) from chat or the API, and nothing may start on Spark 2.
gaps.whyItMatters: Every request that isn't a chat model ends in an explanation today. Verified: the only start verbs are start_model and restart_model, and notBrainsSpark (17-changes.mjs:385) refuses Spark 2. The staged apps draft labels its container spark.console=1 with spark.model and uses host networking, so inventory, /v1/models and the model-start plan would treat an app as a model. The owner's own note (2026-11-11) puts always-on tools on Spark 2.
gaps.proposal: New part /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/19-workloads.mjs; leave the scratchpad 19-apps.mjs unapplied. One saved description (a spec) per workload in STATE_DIR/workload-specs.json with a closed field list: name, kind (service or job), image (pinned by digest at first pull), command, env, files (small text files written into its folder), port, check (an HTTP path that must answer), gpu, memoryGB (required), net (off by default). Three actions: save_workload (changes nothing on the Sparks), run_workload {name, spark?, set?}, stop_workload {name}; extend the existing `workloads` read with specs, state, address and the hub budget. Containers get labels spark.workload and spark.kind, never spark.console; no privileged flag, no host paths, no Docker socket, no host network; two mounts only (its own data folder, the model store read-only); it runs as the owner's uid. gpu:false goes to Spark 2 with --memory, --cpus 4 and a high OOM score, and declared memory there sums to at most a hub budget (6 GB to start). The first run of a spec that isn't built in asks the owner once; a passing check marks it verified and saves any `set` changes, so changing a setting is one sentence. In 16-actions.mjs: add the three to ACTION_KIND, widen the save pattern at line 113, and make tracesToRequest require every word of the name. In 18-workflows.mjs: two WORKFLOWS entries, save_workload in NOT_A_STEP, validateChanged ignores them. In 19-watcher.mjs:57: kind from the label. Tests: test/lib.mjs tool lists, a new test/workload.test.mjs, and test/mock/bin/docker learns the labels. Ship one built-in spec, SearXNG, as the proof.
gaps.risk: A new label that leaks into the model inventory repeats the draft's bug, so one test must assert a workload never appears in running_models or /v1/models. The 6 GB hub budget is a guess until free memory is read on Spark 2 with the brain warm. SearXNG's digest, arm64 build and footprint are unverified. Most of the work is teaching the stand-in docker. It needs the owner's OK to change the rule that nothing but the brain starts on Spark 2.
gaps.dependsOn: The owner's decision on Spark 2 (first owner decision).
gaps.acceptance: In chat: "set up searxng". Sparkie asks once ("Run searxng on Spark 2, about 1 GB, no GPU?"), then answers with its address after the health check. `workloads` shows it as a service; running_models and GET /v1/models don't list it. POST /actions/run_workload {"name":"searxng"} answers that it is already running. "Stop searxng" stops it and keeps its data, and the next start asks nothing.

gaps.gap: Self-healing covers model containers only. A service that crashes, hangs or loses its Spark stays down, and a job cut off by a power loss is never reported.
gaps.whyItMatters: The owner called self-healing huge, and a tool the agents depend on is only useful if it stays up without the owner. Verified: maybeHeal returns unless the kind is 'model' and returns for anything on the brain's Spark (18-workflows.mjs:246-247); healPass works from a should-run list that holds only models and drops Spark 2 (20-desired.mjs:17-21).
gaps.proposal: Three small rules, no new loop. (1) Spark 2 services start with Docker's own --restart unless-stopped, which covers a crash and a Spark 2 reboot with no console code (the brain already relies on it, 13-main-model.mjs:128). (2) In /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-heal.mjs healPass, beside watchBrain, add watchServices: a wanted service that runs but has failed its check for 10 minutes is restarted; one on Spark 3 or 4 that crashed, or whose Spark came back (the existing cameBack and settle time), is started again through run_workload so room is re-checked. Same limits as today: twice in 6 hours, never after out-of-memory, never one the owner stopped. (3) Jobs are never re-run; one that was cut off is reported with its output kept. should_be_running lists wanted services and fleet_events carries the heal lines.
gaps.risk: It is a fourth heal path beside three. If the backlog's single reconcile table lands first, add these as rows there instead. Restarting a service that is slow rather than hung would interrupt it; the 10-minute window and the twice-in-6-hours limit bound that.
gaps.dependsOn: Gap 1.
gaps.acceptance: After Spark 2 restarts, or after the search service crashes, `workloads` shows it running again with a new start time and fleet_events has a healing line; asking Sparkie "what did you fix today?" names it. After "stop searxng" it stays stopped. A service that stops answering is restarted within about 12 minutes, at most twice in 6 hours, and is then reported as held.

gaps.gap: Nothing can run to completion: no script, batch, evaluation or data job, so "write it and run it" is impossible.
gaps.whyItMatters: This is most of "do anything I tell it". Sparkie's tools are the 36 actions and none runs a command or writes a file. The batch work owners describe (extraction, transcribing a folder, evaluations) is a script that calls a model address and exits, and with GLM filling Spark 3 and 4 it has to run on Spark 2.
gaps.proposal: Kind `job` in the same spec and the same three actions, in 19-workloads.mjs. run_workload's operation ends once the container has run 10 seconds, so a multi-hour job doesn't sit in the in-memory operation list (07-jobs.mjs:2), mark its Spark busy (which pauses model healing there) or get lost by a console update; Docker keeps the truth. When the watcher sees the container exit (19-watcher.mjs:99-105), a short job-result operation checks exit code 0 and the declared output file, attaches the last 40 log lines as data and the list of new files, and posts it to the chat that asked. 14-chats.mjs:127 must not carry on while that chat's job still runs, and run_workflow (18-workflows.mjs:193-199) follows a job step until it exits. Past its time limit a job is stopped. One GPU job per Spark; CPU jobs default to Spark 2 under the cap. One built-in spec, `script`: a pinned Python image that runs the files it is given. Network is off unless the spec says net:true, which the first-run question shows.
gaps.risk: This runs code a 27B model wrote. Inside the container it has no keys, no secrets and no path into Spark Console beyond /v1, so it can't lock the owner out; it can waste time, fill its own folder or, with net:true, send out what it can read. A GPU job can pass its declared memory and freeze Spark 3 or 4 until a power cycle (community reports say container limits don't count GPU memory on GB10; not confirmed by NVIDIA). Whether a container on Spark 2's bridge network reaches the console's address needs one check on the Spark. Sparkie's carry-on stops after 2 hours, so a longer job only posts its result.
gaps.dependsOn: Gap 1; the owner's decisions on jobs and on internet access. Scheduled runs come from the backlog's `when` on saved workflows, not from this gap.
gaps.acceptance: In chat: "ask the running model these 20 questions and save the answers to answers.json". Sparkie saves a spec, asks once, and later a result message arrives with exit 0, the last lines and answers.json listed. "Run that again" and POST /actions/run_workload {"name":"questions"} run it with no question. If Spark Console restarts mid-job, the result still arrives within a minute of it coming back. A job past its time limit is reported as stopped, with its output kept.

gaps.gap: A request outside the action list ends in improvisation, and nothing that worked is kept unless the owner says the word "workflow".
gaps.whyItMatters: The owner asked that a first-time request be thought through once and then be a repeatable name for chat and API. Verified: the prompt (14-chats.mjs:40-56) never says what isn't possible; the save pattern (16-actions.mjs:113) only matches "…workflow", so the action's own example "save that as coding mode" comes back as a button; the 29 NVIDIA playbooks already in service/catalog.json are returned by no action.
gaps.proposal: Four small changes. (1) In 14-chats.mjs systemPrompt: one generated line of what isn't possible (built from ACTIONS and the spec store), and the order for a new request: a saved workload or workflow by that name, then a guide, then compose a spec and save it, otherwise say plainly that it can't. (2) In 16-actions.mjs find_recipes: return matching catalog.json playbooks as `guides` (title, link, image, ports), marked as data; guides that install on the host are marked "not runnable here". (3) Line 113 accepts "save that as <name>". (4) When a carried-on request ends with two or more changes that all worked, Spark Console itself saves that chain as a workflow named from the request (never replacing a named one, at most 20 kept), and Sparkie's done line gives the name.
gaps.risk: A looser save pattern could catch "save that file as…": require a name after "as" and add negated and question cases to test/intent.test.mjs. Auto-saved chains can pile up; the cap and never-replace rule bound that. Guide text is outside text and must reach Sparkie as data, never as host commands. Part 4 overlaps the workflows area and should be built once.
gaps.dependsOn: The spec wording in part 1 needs gap 1; parts 2 to 4 stand alone. Carry-on turns (built, in the test gate).
gaps.acceptance: "Set up a vector database" (never done before): Sparkie names the guide it found, saves a spec, asks once and reports the address; the same sentence a week later starts it with no research and no question. "Power off Spark 4" gets "I can't do that; you do it by hand", not a made-up step. After "stop what's on 3 and 4, then start GLM across them" works, `workflows` lists a saved entry, and "save that as coding mode" keeps it under that name without a button.

gaps.gap: Embedding and rerank models can't be started, although the catalog lists them and the gateway already passes /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank.
gaps.whyItMatters: Any agent work over documents needs embeddings. Verified in code: answerTest (09-verified.mjs:28-52) accepts only a chat or plain-completion answer, so such a server would fail with "didn't answer a test prompt" and be put back. This was not run on a Spark, so it is inferred.
gaps.proposal: In /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/09-verified.mjs answerTest: when the recipe's category is embedding or rerank, or chat and completions both come back as unsupported, try /v1/embeddings and then /v1/rerank with a one-line input, and skip the speed measure for those. Extend test/mock/model.mjs and add one test. Speech servers are not vLLM models; they come later as service specs (gap 7).
gaps.risk: A wrong guess of kind could pass a broken chat model: keep the chat check first and fall through only on an "unsupported" answer or a matching category. It changes the start workflow's version, so the next real start is its validation run.
gaps.acceptance: "Start qwen3 embedding on spark 4" finishes with a line saying it answers an embeddings test; GET /v1/models lists it; POST /v1/embeddings with its name returns vectors. A chat model that answers garbage is still refused.

gaps.gap: A model's settings can't be changed from chat or the API: start_model takes only model, spark, sparks and a researched setup id.
gaps.whyItMatters: The owner asked for easily changeable configs. Verified at 17-changes.mjs:499-505. The context-capping code exists but runs only as an out-of-memory fix. This belongs with the models area; it is listed here so it isn't lost between areas.
gaps.proposal: Optional typed inputs on start_model in 17-changes.mjs: context (tokens), parallel (requests at once), quant and engine, mapped through each engine's own flags in 05-library.mjs, nothing free-form. A start with new settings replaces the running copy instead of answering "already", and a run that passes is saved as its own verified setup so "the 64k one" is repeatable. The gate requires the number or word to be in the owner's message, as it already does for Sparks. Workloads get the same through run_workload's `set` (gap 1).
gaps.risk: A setting that doesn't fit ends in the known out-of-memory fix or a put-back. It changes start_model's version, so its next real start validates it.
gaps.acceptance: "Restart gemma with a 64k context and 8 at once" restarts it and the answer states both values as read back from the running server; "start gemma, the 64k one" next week reuses it, and recipe_detail shows it as a verified setup. "Start gemma" with no numbers never invents one.

gaps.gap: GPU services (ComfyUI for images and video, a speech server) can't run, and a model start reserves nothing for a GPU workload that loads its memory later.
gaps.whyItMatters: Images, video and speech are the most common non-LLM uses of a Spark. Verified: plan() (05-library.mjs:181-186) counts only containers holding GPU memory at that moment and memoryShare sizes a model from what is free then, so an idle ComfyUI plus a new model can over-commit and freeze the Spark.
gaps.proposal: Allow gpu:true specs on Spark 3 or 4 only, one per Spark. In 05-library.mjs plan(), a running container labelled spark.workload with gpu counts as holding its declared memoryGB (declared minus used is subtracted from the room in memoryShare) and appears as an optional stop, which is already an owner-only question. Ship no GPU template: ComfyUI, Parakeet or Kokoro are learned as specs when first asked for. An image outside the trusted prefixes (01-setup.mjs:36) is trusted by its digest after the owner's yes, not by widening the list.
gaps.risk: Declared memory is a promise, not a cap: a ComfyUI video workflow can pass it (a forum table reports FLUX.2-dev at 94 GB) and freeze the Spark until someone power-cycles it, and Spark 4 is Wi-Fi only. plan() and memoryShare are in start_model's fingerprint, so it re-validates on its next real start. Community images need arm64 builds; unverified.
gaps.dependsOn: Gaps 1 and 2.
gaps.acceptance: "Set up ComfyUI on Spark 4" ends with its address on port 8188 and a declared memory figure. Then "start gemma on spark 4" either starts gemma in what's left and says so, or asks whether to stop ComfyUI; it never starts both blind. With Spark 4 off, the request says so plainly.

gaps.gap: One console model per Spark: a second one always stops the first, so an embedder, a reranker and a chat model can't share a Spark.
gaps.whyItMatters: A documents stack needs two or three small servers beside a chat model. Verified: every model binds host port 8000 (05-library.mjs:359) and plan() marks any other console model on that Spark as a required stop (line 186).
gaps.proposal: Give each console model its own host port from 8000 up, kept in a spark.port label; in plan() stop another console model only when memory doesn't fit or the owner said switch. Read the port in inventory, restartChecked and the health checks (19 uses of CONFIG.servePort across 7 files in service/src). The gateway already routes by each model's endpoint.
gaps.risk: It touches start, restart and across-Sparks at once, and each needs a validation run. Two engines on one Spark each reserve a share, so the second must be sized after the first has loaded. Beside GLM across Spark 3 and 4 there may be too little memory left for anything (inferred from the 0.9 share cap, not measured), so this mostly helps when the two Sparks run separate models.
gaps.dependsOn: Gap 5.
gaps.acceptance: With a chat model on Spark 3, "start qwen3 embedding on spark 3 too" starts it without stopping the chat model; /v1/models lists both and both answer. When memory is short it refuses, says how much is free and stops nothing.

gaps.gap: No way to hand a job its input files or fetch its output through chat or the API.
gaps.whyItMatters: The only file route is the page's file browser (24-handler.mjs:103), which the backlog removes. Without a replacement a job can work only on what it downloads or what is typed into its spec.
gaps.proposal: Replace the general file browser with one narrow route in 24-handler.mjs: PUT and GET /workloads/<name>/files/<path>, streamed, size-capped, confined to that workload's data folder (resolved path, no symlinks), for the owner and for agent keys allowed to change things. `workloads` lists the folder's files. Build it when the first job needs a file.
gaps.risk: A path check that can be escaped reaches the owner's home folder: resolve inside the folder and add traversal tests. Cap uploads by Content-Length.
gaps.dependsOn: Gap 3; the owner's answer on whether their agents send files.
gaps.acceptance: An agent PUTs notes.zip into the "summarise" job's folder, runs it by name and GETs summaries.json afterwards. A path containing ../ is refused with a clear error.

gaps.gap: A service's own API is reachable only at its Spark's tailnet address and port, with no agent-key check, and speech paths don't pass the gateway.
gaps.whyItMatters: The owner's agents would have to know each service's Spark and port, and an agent calling from the internet can't reach a service at all. Verified: V1_PATHS has five JSON paths and the body must be a JSON object up to 8 MB (15-routes.mjs:144,156-157).
gaps.proposal: One stream-through route in 15-routes.mjs: /svc/<name>/… to a running service's port, with the same key and cross-site checks as /v1 and no body parsing, so uploads work. A spec may list the /v1 paths it serves (for example /v1/audio/transcriptions), which the gateway forwards to it. No /v1/images path: ComfyUI's API isn't OpenAI-shaped. Build it when a speech service is first learned or an agent first calls from off the tailnet.
gaps.risk: An unparsed stream can't be inspected the way JSON is: cap it by Content-Length and forward only to ports registered by a spec, never to an address taken from the request.
gaps.dependsOn: Gap 1.
gaps.acceptance: With an agent key from outside the tailnet, a search request to /console/api/svc/searxng/ returns results; without a key it is refused. Once a speech service runs, an OpenAI client pointed at the one address transcribes a clip.

ownerDecisions: May CPU-only, memory-capped services and jobs run on Spark 2 inside a small hub budget, with GPU work never there? Code, contract section 17 and AGENTS.md:36 forbid every workload on Spark 2; your note of 2026-11-11 puts always-on tools there. Recommendation: yes, 6 GB to start. Without it, gaps 1 to 3 only work while Spark 3 or 4 is on.

Should the brain's memory share go from 0.8 to 0.7 so the hub budget can be the contract's 16 GB? Only you change the brain. Recommendation: not yet. Read free memory on Spark 2 with the brain warm first, and keep 0.8 with a 6 GB budget until a service needs more.

Are jobs acceptable: scripts Sparkie writes, run in a locked container with no keys? A GPU job that runs away could freeze Spark 3 or 4 until it is power-cycled. Recommendation: yes, with the network off by default, your yes on the first run of each new spec, and GPU jobs only on Spark 3 or 4.

May a job or service use the internet while it runs (pip installs, model downloads)? Recommendation: off by default; a spec can ask for it, the first-run question shows it, and your yes there counts as wanting that download.

Which use case first? Recommendation: SearXNG as the first service (it proves the runner and gives your agents search) and one batch script as the first job. Documents, speech and images are learned when you first ask; nothing is pulled ahead of time.

Should a multi-step request that worked be saved automatically, or only offered? Recommendation: saved automatically (at most 20, never replacing one you named), matching your rule that every deploy becomes a recipe because you will forget to ask.

Is 'no training or fine-tuning' (contract section 13, 2026-11-08) still your position, and does it cover quantizing? Recommendation: keep it; seed nothing. If you ask once, it is a job Sparkie learns.

For documents work, should embeddings be always on (a small CPU server on Spark 2, slower) or fast on Spark 3 or 4 (only when they are up, and needing a port per model)? Recommendation: fix the done-check now and decide when you have a real documents use.
Do your agents need to send files to the Sparks, or call services from outside the tailnet? Recommendation: build neither gap 9 nor gap 10 until the first time one is needed.

May Sparkie read web pages found through a search service, treated as data only? Recommendation: yes for looking things up, with one rule: a script whose text came from a page is always shown in the first-run question before it runs.

When the page's routes are removed, models that need their own code or custom flags lose their only way to start (the page's Deploy). Recommendation: keep one owner-only API call for them rather than dropping the ability.
Is Spark 1 coming back into regular use? Recommendation: don't plan around it; if it returns it is the natural home for GPU jobs and ComfyUI, and that lowers the need for a port per model.
disagreements: Shape of the new ability. Inventory: run_job plus three service templates in code. Research: run_job, start_service, stop_service with the spec as data and a separate recipes file. Generic: one spec, two kinds, save/run/stop. I took generic's, with the spec as data and no separate recipes file: the spec store is the recipe store, marked verified on its first passing run.

Where jobs run. Inventory and research put jobs on Spark 3 or 4 inside an engine image with the GPU. Generic defaults CPU jobs to Spark 2. I took generic's: GLM fills both GPU Sparks and most of this owner's jobs are clients of /v1. GPU jobs stay possible on Spark 3 or 4.

verdict: This area is half built. The "repeat" half exists: code records every model start that worked and reuses it, and saved workflows replay a named list of actions from chat, the agent door or POST /actions. title: Truly local and independent (no Mac, no Claude, no cloud needed)
verdict: Spark Console already runs alone for weeks, and with the internet down it keeps the console, the brain, chat, the APIs (from a device already on the tailnet), starts of models on disk, self-healing, saved workflows and memory. It is not yet independent of the Mac: the only complete copy of the code is a Mac folder with no git, the copy on Spark 2 is wiped at every install, the test gate has never run on Linux (I found one place where it will fail there), and nothing in chat or the API can install an update. It is not yet safe for an owner who only chats in one more place: a brain that is stopped or missing is never started again, and chat then points to a page. Tailscale is the one cloud service everything stands on; it stays the owner's by hand, with two settings to switch on and expiry dates shown in fleet_status. Sparkie writing its own fixes is one step further and unproven, because the engine trial is built but has never run. Ten gaps close this, six of them under a day each; the files that matter most are /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/deploy/host-on-portal.sh, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/18-workflows.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-heal.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/05-library.mjs and /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/lock.mjs.
worksToday: Runs alone: one dependency-free Node service under systemd (Restart=always), JSON state, and a daily copy of the state to Spark 3 with the last 14 kept (25-backup-and-start.mjs:6-32, checked).

Internet down: the console, the brain (offline flag, image by id, Docker restarts it after a crash or reboot: 13-main-model.mjs:127-128, checked), chat, the agent door and /v1 from a device already on the tailnet, start/stop/restart of models on disk whose image is on that Spark, self-healing, saved workflows and memory all keep working.

The installer saves a snapshot before every install (10 kept), refuses a server.mjs that does not match its parts, and puts the old build back by itself if the new one does not answer in 45 seconds (host-on-portal.sh:102-227, checked).
undo_update and test_changes are actions; the undo already runs outside the console through systemd-run (18-workflows.mjs:375-406, checked). Built and in the gate, never run on the real Spark 2.
A watchdog timer outside the console restarts it after 3 missed /health checks, at most 3 times an hour (host-on-portal.sh:237-279). Built and in the gate.

Self-healing is bounded and recorded: crashed models, a two-Spark model that lost a part, bring-back after a power-on, and a brain that is running but silent for 10 minutes, each at most twice in 6 hours (20-heal.mjs, checked).
Owner-only questions exist: an agent or a typed yes cannot answer them, and pressing one needs the passkey (22-passkey.mjs:150-154 and 14-chats.mjs:85, checked).
Hugging Face, the image registries and GitHub are needed only for new things; reads are anonymous, fail softly, and a source that fails keeps what earlier looks found.
The engine trial is fully built (agentbar: two engines pinned in one image, four tasks with hidden checks, containers with no Docker socket or keys). It has only ever run dry.
The console's private socket is readable only by the owner's account and is what Tailscale itself uses (25-backup-and-start.mjs:56-58), so checks from Spark 2 itself need no network.

gaps.whyItMatters: A lost Mac disk loses the source for good, and nothing can be changed, tested or installed without the Mac. Every other gap here stands on the code living on Spark 2 with its history. The stale lock is a live trap: the installer only checks that workflows.lock.json exists (host-on-portal.sh:26), while the service counts a workflow as tested only when the lock's build equals its own (18-workflows.mjs:81). One install at the wrong moment switches every start, stop and crash restart off while /health still says ok. I checked: the tree's build is c0789b85fa67 and the lock says 58650129ef9b while the gate runs.

Ship this first. 3) Replace the source swap (lines 229-236): the first install runs git init in ~/spark-console-src; every healthy install replaces the files but leaves .git, commits, and tags installed/<build>. Track the built server.mjs and the lock, so a tag is exactly what was installed. The snapshot notes its commit, and restore.sh moves the checkout back to it, so undo_update takes the source back too. 4) install.sh refuses a Mac install based on an older commit than Spark 2's ("Spark 2 has changes this Mac doesn't: pull first"). 5) /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs: add a git bundle of the code to the daily copy, and try the copy again when the target Spark comes back instead of tomorrow. /health gains the installed commit.

One download on Spark 2 for the gate and engine image (about 1-1.5 GB: Node 24, a few packages, two engines). Recommend yes once, and being asked again for each engine version bump.

Should an update install without a button once the gate passes? Recommend: yes for an update you asked for and for changes you or your agents pushed. For code Sparkie wrote itself, one plain button until the three drills and the first few changes have been seen; then you switch it to install and report after. Changes to sign-in, SSH, deploy, the test harness or the brain's config always wait for your passkey.

Must every changed line in an existing test wait for you? Recommend: removing or changing an existing check waits; adding a new action's name to the tool lists in test/lib.mjs does not, or nearly every new feature would ask.

Does the Mac stay as a way to install? Recommend: it becomes an optional git clone that pushes to Spark 2 and calls update_console. Remove the tar path in host-on-portal.sh after two clean self-updates.

disagreements: Where the gate runs. deps: on Spark 2's own Node, started with systemd-run, with an environment override for the releases folder. selfchange and the earlier backlog: in the agentbar image with no network. I took the container: on the hub that runs the brain, no network and no Docker socket mean a missed stand-in cannot touch the real machine, and it fixes the Node version and the releases tests with no code. Effort for the gate. Both sub-agents said S. I raised it to M: the suite has never run on Linux, and I found a break neither reported (the stand-in Sparks read the real /proc/meminfo on any Linux machine, 05-library.mjs:52 and :335), which fails the memory tests on the host and in the container alike.

title: Self-healing and fixing things by itself
verdict: Restarting is solid; telling the owner and fixing new failures are not. Of 17 failure cases, six heal by themselves today, and healing never needs the brain and never touches SSH, Tailscale, the firewall or users, which is the right base. For an owner who uses only chat and the API, with no notifications, four things fall short: a brain that is down is never brought back and takes chat with it; a heal can go against the owner's latest wish (stop a newer model, bring back a stale one, cut the context to 8k); a one-Spark heal skipped for a passing reason is never retried; and nothing lists what is open. "Fixing by itself" ends at four coded fixes: a start that fails in a new way is put back and forgotten, with no diagnosis, no lever for Sparkie, and nothing learned for the next chat or API call. The plan is ten changes, mostly re-wiring and deletion (one pass in place of three loops, one open-problems list worked out from live state, a brain keeper, a safer installer, then try_fix and one small file of learned fixes), with no new service or engine; build gaps 2, 3 and 5 first (each under a day), then 1 and 4, then 6 and 7 behind an eval on the real brain, then 8 to 10. Critical files: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-heal.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/17-changes.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/19-watcher.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/deploy/host-on-portal.sh.
worksToday: Console crash: systemd starts it again in 3 seconds (Restart=always).
Console hang: a watchdog outside the console restarts it after 3 missed minutes, at most 3 times an hour (built and in the test gate, not installed yet).

Sparkie's model crash or Spark 2 reboot: Docker's own restart policy brings the container back (warm start about 51 s). Running but silent for 10 minutes: the console restarts it, at most twice in 6 hours.
A one-Spark model that crashes: restarted as it was with a room check and a test prompt, at most twice an hour, never stopping anything else.
A two-Spark model that loses a part: what is left stops and the pair starts again with its cable and engine checks and the known fixes; if the start is refused, the part that was stopped comes back.

Spark 3 or 4 powered off and on: seen within 30 seconds, counted only after 90 seconds off, waits 2 minutes to settle, then brings back what should run, once per power-on; held if the Spark went down within 30 minutes of the last bring-back.

A failed start puts back what it stopped. Nine failure kinds are recognised and four are fixed automatically (plain sockets instead of RoCE, a shorter context, dropping a rejected flag, one more try at an image pull).
A start that needed a fix is saved with that fix (verified.json) and reused first for the same model.
An update that fails its first 45 seconds is put back by the installer; the last 10 installs are kept as snapshots.
State files are written atomically; unreadable recipes, memory, should-run and saved workflows are set aside with a notice; a daily copy of the state goes to another Spark (14 kept).
Healing runs without the brain, obeys the owner's pause (not an agent's automatic pause), keeps its attempt counts on disk across restarts, and is not counted against the agents' safety pause.
Held models are in Sparkie's notes, and Sparkie can bring one back with restart_model or start_model. Every action also works through the API while the brain is down.

What a heal nobody asked for may give up. Recommend: nothing except plain sockets instead of RoCE on the cable (same model, slower), said in open problems. Never a shorter context, and a model that ran out of memory stays held until you ask.
After a power cycle, your latest start on a Spark wins over an older should-run entry for that Spark (gap 2). Recommend yes.

The 30-minute "Spark was offline" rule for crash restarts. Recommend keeping it, but as a wait that ends by itself. The other choice, a 90-second rule that ignores Wi-Fi blips, heals sooner but means replacing a pinned test, which needs your sign-off.

title: Chat and the API can do everything
verdict: Chat and the API already cover the model side of the fleet: 36 actions (23 lookups, 13 changes), the same list for Sparkie, the agent door and POST /actions/<name>, which I confirmed is already in service/src and server.mjs, not just staged. Against "do anything I tell it", three things are missing: the owner's own API and chat calls are still treated as an agent's in five places; nothing Sparkie did is kept exactly, so "remember it and repeat it" rests on a 27B model's recall; and there is no action for a config change, a download on its own, anything that isn't a model server, or an update of the console. Six paths are still page-only or SSH-only (resume after a pause, start a stopped brain, forget a held model, add a recipe, test the cable, delete a model). Gaps 1 to 6 are small or medium and close everything about models, configs, pairs, repeating and recovery; the two large ones (a sandboxed job launcher and update_console) decide whether "anything" and "independent" are really true, and both need an owner decision first. Self-healing improves along the way: it brings back the setup the owner chose, starts a dead brain, and one why_failed lookup gives Sparkie the cause and the next call. Critical files, all under /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src: 16-actions.mjs, 17-changes.mjs, 18-workflows.mjs, 14-chats.mjs, 24-handler.mjs.
worksToday: One action list for every door: Sparkie's tools, the MCP door (/mcp) and POST /actions/<name> all run the same 36 actions through runAction (checked in /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/24-handler.mjs:221-229 and server.mjs:7049).

Start, stop and restart with their checks, known fixes and put-back; a model not on disk is downloaded and started in one operation; Recipes models start across Spark 3 and 4 when the cable test says full.
Saved workflows by name (save_workflow, run_workflow, forget_workflow) from chat, the door and the API; each step runs as its own validated action and the first failure ends the run.

Memory (remember, forget_memory, memory) at the end of Sparkie's prompt, and Sparkie carrying a multi-step owner request on after its operations finish (both built and in the test gate, not installed).

Self-healing: a crashed one-Spark model restarts, a two-Spark model that lost a part starts again as a pair, what should run comes back at power-on, a running but silent brain is restarted; should_be_running shows what is held and why.
Cancel and undo inside a chat; test_changes and undo_update as actions (in the gate).
The gateway passes through /v1/chat/completions, completions, responses, embeddings and rerank (15-routes.mjs:144).
Outside agents talk to Sparkie with ask_sparkie, take its choices by id, and owner-only questions are answered with the passkey button in chat (22-passkey.mjs:149-152).
Diagnosis lookups: fleet_events, workloads, container_logs, operation_log, spark_diagnostics, service_logs.
The cable test runs by itself every 10 minutes (a few pings, changes nothing) and linked_sparks reads the last result.

ownerDecisions: 1. Should a POST /actions call that carries your own Tailscale identity count as your own hand (not stopped by the agents' pause, not counted toward it)? Recommend yes; agents that should be limited use a key on /mcp.

2. One pause switch or two? Recommend one: your pause stops Sparkie, agents and healing; the automatic pause stops only agents and Sparkie's carried-on turns. Remove the separate self-heal switch. The brain's own watch keeps running under either.
3. May Sparkie, on your word in your own chat, cancel an operation that self-healing, another chat or an outside agent started? Recommend yes.

4. Is a sandboxed container job (run_job on Spark 3 or 4) wanted, given the contract lists training and fine-tuning as not wanted? Recommend yes to the generic job, no to any fine-tune feature, and an app only when you name one. Reword the Spark 2 rule to 'no GPU workload on Spark 2'.

6. Deleting models: allowed at all? Recommend yes, only as a passkey button in chat, never through the API or an agent.

7. Gated models: recommend you run hf auth login once on Spark 3 and once on Spark 4 by hand (no code, no token handled by the console). Build the copy-from-Spark-2 step only if gated models become common.

8. Should an agent key work on /mcp from a Spark's own address (an agent living on Spark 2)? Today it is refused while the same key works from the internet. Recommend allowing it only when the request carries a valid key, and only if you plan to run agents on Spark 2; it touches the request gate, so it is your call.
9. Schedules: recommend a scheduled workflow never downloads and never answers a question for you; a step that would do either fails and says so.
10. Power: should 'shut down Spark 4' be an action? Recommend not now: it needs a sudo rule you would add by hand, and powering back on still needs a hand.

title: Easily changeable configs
verdict: Configs are the weakest part of "do anything I tell it": through chat or the API the owner can pick a model, its Sparks and a Recipes setup id, and nothing else. There is no input for context, requests at once, memory share, engine, image or flags, and asking for new settings on a model that is already running is answered "already running; nothing changed". Fleet settings sit in config.json, which ships as code and is overwritten by every install; the self-healing switch needs the page and a passkey, and once the 12-changes-an-hour pause trips, a chat-and-API-only owner has no way to resume. The pieces to fix this already exist (verified.json is a store of setups that worked, agent-settings.json is a live settings file, POST /actions/<name> is in the source), so the plan is nine small changes on existing machinery, not a config system. Three safety holes must close in the same batch as the new inputs, or a changed setting can cost the owner the working one: a one-Spark re-start deletes the old container before the new one is proven, a fix's cut-down run can become the default, and healing and undo restart a two-Spark model with the fastest known setup instead of the one that ran. The brain's engine flags stay preset-only and owner-only by terminal command; nothing here can reach SSH, addresses, ports or users.
worksToday: start_model takes a model in the owner's words, one Spark or two linked Sparks, and a Recipes setup id; the gate understands 'on 3' and 'across 3 and 4' (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/17-changes.mjs:496-505).

Every start that answers is recorded in verified.json with its engine, image, flags, environment, Spark count and measured speed, and the next plain start reuses the fastest one (09-verified.mjs:91-114, 17-changes.mjs:161-177).
Nine known start failures have fixes that are tried by themselves, up to 3 attempts in 30 minutes, and what was stopped to make room is started again on failure (17-changes.mjs:191-302, 311-325).
A two-Spark re-start sets the old parts aside under another name and puts them back if the new one fails (08-cluster.mjs:349-385).
A crashed one-Spark model heals by restarting the same container, so its settings survive (20-heal.mjs:98).

Every setup and every past run is re-checked before it runs: unsafe flags and environment variables are dropped or refused, images must come from the trusted list, and remote code needs the owner (service/dig.mjs:206-290, 11-setups.mjs:283-316).
The memory share is measured at each start and 8 GB is always kept free (05-library.mjs:297-316).

Memory (remember, forget_memory) and saved workflows (save, run, forget) change by saying so, are read live from the state folder, and need no restart; a saved workflow's steps run without the word check, so it can carry a placement.
The pause and the self-healing switch are read live from agent-settings.json at each use; an automatic pause can be lifted without a passkey (17-changes.mjs:15-31, 22-passkey.mjs:148).

POST /actions/<name> is in the source and built (24-handler.mjs:221-229, applied 08:51 today, its tests passed at 08:55): it runs as the owner's own call, counts as a validation run and is not counted toward the 12 changes an hour.
The brain switches between presets by id through /main/use and goes back by itself if the new one does not start (13-main-model.mjs:249-268).

ownerDecisions: Should settings you ask for become that model's usual setup as soon as they work? Recommended: yes, with once for a try and 'best' to go back; the reply always says which setup it used.

Free-form flags on start_model: who may pass them? Recommended: your chat when the flag is literally in your message (otherwise one button), your own API calls, and your agents that may change things. Every flag passes the same check as a recipe from the web; environment variables never.
Is '64k' 65,536 tokens or 64,000? Recommended: 65,536, converted by the console and stated in the reply, so the engines' different readings of k do not matter.
Turning self-healing on or off without the passkey. Recommended: yes, a plain audited setting; contract 8.7 does not list it and the passkey step today comes from a path rule.
While agents are paused, should your own POST /actions calls still go through, and should 'resume' in chat be one button? Recommended: yes to both; Sparkie and agent keys can never resume themselves.

The 12 changes an hour also count your own requests through Sparkie. Recommended: keep 12 and keep counting, but make it a setting you can raise with one API call; revisit if it trips in normal use once Sparkie carries requests on.
May Sparkie change its own thinking, reply length, tool rounds or changes per turn when you say so in chat? Recommended: it shows a button; your direct API call changes them at once.
The tuned brain preset from the review: replace aphex-agent-fast or sit beside it? Recommended: beside it as a third preset you switch to with one command, with aphex and aphex-x4 deleted.

Do you want two models on one Spark soon (for example a chat model plus an embedding model)? Recommended: not in this batch. Each Spark has one model port and a start stops any other console model there, so a memory share alone will not do it; per-model ports would have to come first.

The Spark list has two homes (config.json and access.json's nodes). Which one is live on Spark 2 needs one read of access.json there. Recommended: keep config.json as the only home and remove the other; changing it stays a hand edit.
disagreements: Free-form flags. The inventory report wants a flags input checked by cleanFlags; the design report wants six typed fields only and cites contract 6.14. I took both: typed fields first, plus flags as a checked escape hatch. 6.14's last sentence says its limits are for variants nobody asked for, the flags get the same check web recipes already pass with one click, and without them 'anything I tell it' ends at the fields we thought of (tool-call parser, reasoning parser, cache type). Environment variables stay out.

title: Combining Sparks
verdict: For this fleet, combining Sparks means one model across Spark 3 and Spark 4. That works today, heals as a pair, and runs at NVIDIA's published two-Spark speed, so three or four Sparks, replicas and a scheduler are not worth building for one owner. The gaps are all about GPU Sparks that are switched on and off: self-healing can stop a newer model to bring an older one back, a Spark that is off makes its models vanish (wrong refusals, and a second download of a model that already exists), and a pair that loses one Spark is ignored and still reported as running. The owner's pair sentences (restart, switch, move, say it twice) are refused or take several rounds, which is also why a layout can't yet be saved once and repeated by name from chat or the API. Turning a Spark off can ship now; turning one on needs two smart plugs, because NVIDIA confirms there is no Wake-on-LAN. Gaps 1 to 5 and 9 need no hardware and add one idea at most; the rest waits on the owner's decisions or the plugs. The files that matter most are 20-heal.mjs, 20-desired.mjs, 17-changes.mjs, 15-routes.mjs and 18-workflows.mjs under /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src.
worksToday: One Recipes model across Spark 3 + Spark 4 with vLLM or SGLang, started from chat ("run X across 3 and 4"), the agent door, or POST /actions/start_model with sparks. GLM-5.3 Flash is validated at about 28 tok/s; the Qwen proof run (22 tok/s) matches NVIDIA's published two-Spark figure, so the cable performs as designed.
Placement picks one Spark if the model fits, else a pair whose cable tested good. The cable and engine checks run before anything stops, and a start that never connects is retried over plain sockets.
One stop_model stops both parts of a pair. With one Spark off it still stops the part that is left (read in 07-jobs.mjs stopContainer, not run).

A pair that loses a part while both Sparks stay on is restarted as a pair. After a power-on, what should run comes back once the Sparks have settled, once per power-on, with a hold if a Spark goes down again within 30 minutes.
The one address (/console/api/v1) routes by model name to wherever it runs, starts a model on a call when nothing has to stop, and passes /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank through.

Read-only helpers work from chat and the API: cluster_plan (dry run), linked_sparks (last cable test, repeated every 10 minutes and kept on disk), where_it_fits, should_be_running (with held and why), and running_models (says whether each model is answering).

ownerDecisions: 1. May self-healing stop the leftover half of a pair when its other Spark is off? The contract says the loop never stops anything. Recommend yes, only when the Spark is offline and its cable port is down, since a pair can't work with the cable down.

2. Does the newer request win? A start on a Spark would take a held model that needs that Spark off the should-run list, and "stop X" on a held model would take it off too. Recommend yes, with the reply saying what left the list; undo restores it.

3. May a start that names a Spark stop a pair holding that Spark, and may a saved workflow stop a model that answered a call in the last 30 minutes without asking? Recommend yes for the owner's own words and saved workflows; an agent's own start still asks.

4. When Spark 3 and 4 power on, should the last layout come back by itself after two minutes (today's behaviour, a 12-minute load for GLM)? Recommend keeping it; with decision 2 a newer start simply replaces it.

5. Smart plugs: buy two with power metering and a local HTTP API (no cloud) and give them fixed LAN addresses. Pull Spark 4's power once to confirm the MSI unit boots when power returns. Recommend keeping any plug password in a 0600 file on Spark 2 (it is a device secret, not the owner's password) and never listing a plug for Spark 2.
6. Run deploy/power-setup.sh once for Spark 3 and 4. It adds a sudo rule for exactly two commands and has --undo. Recommend yes; gap 6 needs it, and it stays an owner-run step.
7. Should an API call to a model whose Sparks are off power them on? Recommend no: the call answers that they are off, and only the owner's words or a saved workflow turn Sparks on.

8. May a small embedder and reranker run on Spark 2? Recommend yes, as a CPU-only app with a memory cap, not through start_model, and without lowering the brain's memory share. Decide when a RAG or voice use case is actually wanted.
9. Spark 4's wired port shows no carrier, so it is on Wi-Fi only. Recommend fixing the cable or port by hand over any code workaround; it makes "unreachable" mean "off".

10. Which cables are plugged in today? The docs and the fleet notes say Spark 2, 3 and 4 form a three-way mesh; the brief names only the 3-4 cable. Asking Sparkie "which Sparks are linked?" settles it. It affects copy speed and any later plan for Spark 1.
11. Spark 1 is locked out and every scan tries it and fails. Recommend removing it from config.json until the login is recovered; adding it back is one entry.

12. Keep the two-Spark Qwen path built from the brain's setup without its draft model? At about 22 tok/s it is slower than the brain on one Spark. Recommend keeping it as the proof that the cable works, with the reply saying it is slower.

title: The brain and its agent loop
verdict: The brain is the right model on the right machine, and the loop in 14-chats.mjs has the right shape (typed actions, a gate that checks the owner's words, changes run in order, results posted back), so one clear request works today. Against "do anything I tell it", three things I confirmed in the code fall short: a multi-step request silently stops half-way whenever an operation finishes before Sparkie's reply does (the common case), Sparkie cannot see its own earlier reasoning or tool calls so it cannot turn what it just did into a workflow without retyping it from prose, and a saved workflow can run on any message that merely contains a start verb. Against "self-healing", the brain itself is the weak spot: nothing checks that it answers correctly at 4 at once (I confirmed the upstream report of wrong answers under parallel load on this exact model, quantization, draft and cache type, closed with no fix), and a brain whose container is gone or stopped is never brought back while the chat points to a page the owner no longer uses. There is also no line for the owner: agents' calls reach the engine uncounted and uncapped, and the eval that should guard all of this has 16 one-message cases and one recorded run. Ten changes close it, most under a day, with no new store and no brain restart until the last one. Work that no action covers at all (a general "do this new thing" step) is the workflows area's to design, and should wait until carry-on, the record and the eval make this loop trustworthy.
worksToday: One clear request in chat: start, stop or restart runs straight away only when the owner's words name that kind of change and that target; anything less clear comes back as one button (service/src/16-actions.mjs sparkieCheck, runAction).

Inside one reply, lookups run together and changes run one after another in the order asked; at most 4 calls a round, each result cut at 12,000 characters, each tool given 50 seconds (service/src/14-chats.mjs:287-327).
A closed page or locked phone no longer cuts a turn; it finishes and is saved (14-chats.mjs:365).
Operation results are posted into the chat that started them (postResult), and numbers in an answer that no tool returned are flagged.
Carry-on (built, in the gate) works when the operation outlasts Sparkie's reply, such as a long model start; it acts only on the owner's stored words and stops after 8 turns or 2 hours.
Memory (built, in the gate): up to 40 short lines at the end of Sparkie's prompt, each now shown with its id; only the owner's own words add or remove one.
Saved workflows: named steps with {inputs}, each step run as its own validated workflow; agents can run one by name through the MCP door.

The brain: aphex-agent-fast, thinking on, 262K context, 4 at once. A failed switch goes back to the previous setup; a brain that is running but silent for 10 minutes is restarted (at most twice in 6 hours); Docker brings it back after a crash or reboot.
The /v1 gateway refuses fields that would run a caller's code and refuses model names it doesn't serve instead of quietly answering with the brain.
The agents' safety pause trips at 12 changes in an hour or three failed operations in a row, and never needs a passkey to resume.

I confirmed the race: the task is saved only when the reply ends (14-chats.mjs:337), a finished operation looks for it at once (:127), and a new message clears it first (:190). A stop takes seconds; a thinking reply takes 10 to 60 s. So the stop's result is posted and nothing follows, with no word to the owner. The test passes only because the stand-in model answers instantly. Four more silent stops, also confirmed: a first step that needs a button sets no task; a typed "yes" clears the task (the page's button does not); a refused carry-on only writes to the console log; a console restart (a self-update) loses it.

ownerDecisions: Install the batch now in the gate as it is, or hold it until carry-on is fixed? Recommendation: install it if the gate passes (memory, test and undo of updates, the source on Spark 2 and the watchdog all matter for independence), treat carry-on as not working yet, and make gap 1 the first change of the next build.

If the brain check finds wrong answers at 4 at once with the draft model, which gives way: speed or parallel work? Recommendation: decide from the measured numbers, leaning to running without the draft at 4 at once until an SGLang release fixes it, because a wrong tool call costs more than a slower one.

Reserve one of the four brain slots for your own chat, leaving agents three? Recommendation: yes. It is what meets the 3-second first-words bar while agents hammer, and the cost halves if 8 at once ever arrives.

Should a finished multi-step request be kept as a draft workflow by itself, or only when you say "save that as …"? Recommendation: by itself, at most 10 drafts, dropped after 30 days unused, with one line in the reply naming the draft. That matches "think once, then repeat".
May your agents bring the brain back with start_sparkie (the saved setup only, never a switch)? Recommendation: yes for agents allowed to change things; it is what lets the API fix a dead chat.

Sampling and thinking depth: the model card gives temperature 1.0 for thinking; the live setup uses 0.6 at full effort. Recommendation: let the eval choose one value for the whole setup, and change only if it passes all three runs more often.

8 at once? Recommendation: not until the check passes at 4, stage 1 has been stable for days, linger is on for Spark 2, and the counter shows your agents actually wait at 4. If they never queue, it buys nothing.

Remove the old presets (aphex 1M context, aphex-x4, aphex-agent) and the YaRN overlay? Tests pin them, and the rules forbid weakening tests without your yes. Recommendation: yes, once the tuned setup is the saved one, keeping one predecessor as the way back. You lose the one-line way to a 1M context.

May your real chats on Spark 2 become eval cases, and should conversations your agents start through ask_sparkie carry on too? Recommendation: yes to both. The chats stay on Spark 2; agents' carry-on comes after it is proven in your own chat, with the same budget, acting on the agent's stored message.
